task.title: Latest-request search controller
task.specification: config={} . Initially mounted=true,query='',current=null,loading=false,result=null,error=null. search={type:'search',id,query} while mounted cancels a loading current request (effect {type:'cancel',id}), sets the new query/current, loading=true,error=null and emits {type:'request',id,query}; prior result remains visible. Issued IDs are unique within an instance, queries may repeat. success={type:'success',id,result} or failure={type:'failure',id,error} only settles a mounted, loading, matching current request. Success replaces result and clears error; failure sets error and retains result. Both stop loading. cancel stops a loading request and emits its cancel effect, clears current and error, retaining query/result. dispose does the same cancellation then resets all data to initial values except mounted=false. mount resets to initial mounted state only when previously disposed. All other events while disposed are ignored. Output {mounted,query,current,loading,result,error,effects}; effects occur only on the current event, in cancel-before-request order. Late errors after success are ignored. Return one output per event. State is opaque JSON, initially null. Output objects have exactly the documented keys; object key order is irrelevant, array order is significant. IDs are nonempty ASCII strings. Values are JSON scalars unless stated otherwise. Numeric values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; integral JSON notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values without unpaired surrogates. Inputs have at most 48 events and eight simultaneous identities. Ordinary instances vary values; boundary instances emphasize empty/disabled/equality/no-op states; adversarial instances reorder callbacks and interleave edits; shift instances use longer traces/more identities within the same rules. These tasks test controller state/effects only, not visual quality, browser integration or screen-reader usability.

matchedCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
matchedCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
matchedCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
matchedCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

shuffledCard.label: Seed banking
shuffledCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
shuffledCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

initial.explanation: The conditional rule is: callbacks affect state only when the controller is mounted, still loading, and the callback ID equals the current request ID. A new search cancels the prior loading request before issuing its request; disposed instances ignore everything except mount.
initial.mapping: The rule maps request identity and lifecycle state to visible state transitions and ordered effects: current identifies the sole settleable request, loading gates settlement, mounted gates all activity, and effects records only cancellations and requests from the current event.
initial.assumptions: Events use the documented types and fields. State is trusted only as the state previously returned by this function; null means the documented initial mounted state. JSON values are finite and directly reusable.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){function eq(a,b){if(a===b)return true;if(!a||!b||typeof a!==typeof b)return false;if(Array.isArray(a))return Array.isArray(b)&&a.length===b.length&&a.every((v,i)=>eq(v,b[i]));if(typeof a==='object'){let ka=Object.keys(a),kb=Object.keys(b);if(ka.length!==kb.length)return false;return ka.every(k=>Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(b,k)&&eq(a[k],b[k]))}return false} let s=null,r=[];for(let e of input.events){let x=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:e});s=x.state;r.push(x.output)}return eq(r,output)}

final.explanation: Callbacks settle only when mounted, loading, and their ID matches the current request. Searches cancel any active request before issuing a new one. Cancel and dispose cancel active work; dispose resets data and marks the controller disposed. Disposed controllers ignore all events except mount.

initial.explanation: Maintain an opaque controller state. Only the mounted, loading request matching the current ID may settle; a new search cancels the prior request first. Disposal resets data and unmounts, while mount restores the initial mounted state.
initial.mapping: The current ID is the causal identity of the active request; query/result/error/loading are retained or replaced exactly as specified, and effects record only cancellation and request actions from the current event.
initial.assumptions: Events are legal JSON objects under the stated contract. Unknown events are no-ops while mounted and all non-mount events are no-ops while disposed.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||typeof x!=="object"||Array.isArray(x))return false;for(const k of ["mounted","query","current","loading","result","error","effects"])if(!(k in x))return false;if(Object.keys(x).length!==7||!Array.isArray(x.effects))return false}return true}

final.explanation: The controller preserves the initial data model, tracks only the latest loading request, and emits effects for cancellation and request issuance in order. Settlements are accepted only for the mounted, loading request whose ID matches current. Results persist across searches, failures, and cancellation as required. Disposal cancels any active request, resets data, and unmounts; only mount restores the initial mounted state.

initial.explanation: Latest-request causality: only the mounted request whose ID is current and loading may settle. New searches cancel the prior request first; disposal cancels and resets.
initial.mapping: State tracks mounted, query, current request ID, loading, result, and error. Each event produces post-event state plus only that event's effects.
initial.assumptions: Events use type search, success, failure, cancel, dispose, or mount. Result and error values may be any JSON value.

final.explanation: Tracks the mounted lifecycle and latest request causality. Only a loading request matching the current ID may settle. Searches cancel the active request before issuing a new one; cancellation and disposal preserve or reset data as specified, while disposed instances ignore all events except mount.
